result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): Answer A covers every part of the guarantee: what it covers, how long, how to claim and what Halyard does. Every term the brief didn't give is a visible placeholder, so the owner can't publish a promise they didn't choose. Answer B's copy is richer, but it writes invented terms into the main text (30 days, 1 year, no deposit, paying for damage) and only labels them as suggestions in the notes below, and the damage promise could be hard for a two-person crew to keep. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B gives usable guarantee copy with a clear claim method, a return visit and a refund, and it leaves days, contact details and the refund amount as visible brackets for the owner to fill in, so it matches the rubric's main requirement closely. A is warmer and covers more ground (pay after the work, no surprise charges, damage cover), but it writes 30 days and 1 year into the live copy and only flags them as suggestions later. A also promises to pay for damage, which depends on insurance the brief never mentions. A also lacks a claim step, and its broad 'if you're not happy' promise isn't tied to a time limit in the headline.
